annotations.count_cue: 595 poems = 591 distinct Roman-numbered poem-headers (bare /^[IVXLC]+$/ lines inside the poem-body span [proem→back-matter], each followed by a verse body) + 4 unnumbered section-opening PROEMS leading PART ONE/TWO/THREE/FIVE (PART FOUR opens directly at numbered I). RECONCILED 2026-06-19 via the per-instance materializer (.scratch/mask-eval/instance_edges.py, count gate GREEN at 595): the prior 589 was a max-numeral estimate, but this B&N edition merges multiple source collections and numbers NON-MONOTONICALLY (e.g. PART FIVE runs …CXXX, CXXXXI=141, CXXXII=132…), so the count of distinct numbered headers (591) exceeds the highest numeral reached. Excluded: the 'FROM THE PAGES OF…' front-matter header and verses quoted in the INTRODUCTION. NOTE: a raw /^[IVXLC]+$/ count over the WHOLE text yields ~1187 — those are the front CONTENTS + back INDEX OF FIRST LINES re-listing the numerals, NOT body poems; the body-span filter isolates the 591 true headers (the earlier 'standalone I pronoun' explanation was wrong).

annotations.note: 595 poems across 5 parts. The 4 named proems: 'This is my letter to the world' (ONE), 'My nosegays are for captives' (TWO), "It's all I have to bring to-day" (THREE), 'One sister have I in our house' (FIVE) — note the BODY renders the first word small-caps (MY/IT's/ONE), so body anchors differ from the lowercase index forms. Per-instance edges DONE 2026-06-19 (count gate GREEN at 595). A2/A3 vs detector: boundary accuracy 99.0% (589/595 gold edges land exactly on a detector boundary), but assignment 0% correct — the detector types every poem as `header` (589) or `chapter` (5), never `poetry`. The mask-type assignment, not the boundary, is the real defect.
